title: As a recruiter, I run configurable hiring pipelines — custom stages per job, drag-to-move candidates, and bulk actions across the whole pipeline
As a recruiter, every candidate has one unified profile — resume, email threads, interview feedback, activity history, and consent status in a single record
As a hiring manager, the hiring team collaborates in the ATS — @mentions, shared notes, tasks, and visibility rules that keep sensitive feedback scoped
As an operations lead, job openings and offers route through configurable approval chains before anything goes live or gets sent
As a founder, I get a hosted, branded careers page on my own domain — jobs publish to it straight from the ATS with no engineering work
As a recruiter, one posting fans out to the job boards — LinkedIn, Indeed, and the aggregators — with sponsored-post management from inside the ATS
As a recruiter, application forms are mine to shape — custom questions, knockout rules, and EEOC/demographic collection handled compliantly
As a recruiter, candidates self-schedule from live calendar availability — booking links tied to my team's calendars end the timezone email chains
As a recruiter, multi-interviewer panels and full onsite loops schedule automatically — interviewer load balancing, room booking, and conflict resolution included
As a hiring manager, interviewers get prepared automatically — calendar invites carry the interview kit, the scorecard, and reminders to submit feedback
As a hiring manager, interviews are scored on structured scorecards — defined attributes per stage, focused rubrics per interviewer, comparable across candidates
As a recruiter, each role carries an interview plan — stages, question banks, and per-interviewer focus areas defined once and reused
As an operations lead, the platform helps reduce bias — structured feedback ordering, demographic-blind review options, and DEI reporting on the funnel
As a recruiter, sourcing lives in a talent CRM — pools of prospects, personalized email sequences with tracking, and nurture campaigns for future roles
As an employee, I can refer candidates through a real referral flow — submit, track status, and see where my referral stands
As a recruiter, a browser extension captures prospects from LinkedIn and the web straight into the ATS with deduplication
As a recruiter, offers go out from the ATS — templated offer letters with dynamic fields, approval routing, and built-in e-signature
As an operations lead, a signed offer flows into onboarding — HRIS and payroll integrations carry the new hire's data over without re-entry
As a founder, I see the hiring funnel honestly — stage conversion, time-to-hire, source effectiveness, and offer-accept rates per role and team
As an analyst, I can build custom reports and get the data OUT — scheduled exports, BI connectors, or a documented reporting API to my warehouse
As a recruiter, AI helps screen and match candidates against the role — with the vendor documenting how it works and what safeguards apply to automated decisions
As a hiring manager, interviews get AI notes and summaries — recorded, transcribed, and distilled into the scorecard with candidate consent handled
As a recruiter, AI drafts the words — job descriptions, outreach sequences, and rejection notes generated in my tone from the role's context
